item.title: [7] Tuning La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 magnetic anisotropy via interfacial coupling in homometallic trilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Luigi Maritato, Alice Galdi

Authors: Nunzia Coppola, Giovanni Vinai, Alksandr Yu Petrov, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnetic anisotropy and exchange bias in complex oxide heterostructures.

Tags: #experiment #LSMO #heterostructure

Abstract: In this work we explore the complex magnetic behaviour of SrMnO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/SrMnO3 trilayers combining magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) and magneto-resistance measurements. The interplay of structural and orbital reconstruction and the competition of ferromagnetism/antiferromagnetism at the interfaces is responsible of a variety of complex magnetic properties, highlighting the use of heterostructures as an effective strategy to tune and control magnetic behaviour. We demonstrate the possibility to tune the magnetic properties of a ferromagnetic La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 (LSMO) layer, embedded in two homometallic antiferromagnetic layers (SrMnO3, SMO), by properly varying the role of interfaces using two different LSMO thickness values. Spin reorientation of the LSMO magnetic easy axis away from its room temperature orientation was observed below 125 K, due to the predominance of exchange interaction at the interface over the substrate-induced magnetic anisotropy, in agreement with established models for homometallic manganite heterostructures. The competition of super-exchange and exchange interactions at the interface results in a highly frustrated interfacial spin glass state, resulting in 20-fold enhancement of the coercive field and exchange bias. The modification of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy driven by the interfacial effects leads to a change in the anisotropic magneto-resistance response of the system, which dominates the low temperature behaviour.

item.title: [9] A B1g phonon unlocks d-wave superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Zhi-Xun Shen, Thomas P. Devereaux

Authors: Wen O. Wang, Tianshu Li, Xiaoyue Ma, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Zhi-Xun Shen

Tags: #STS #superconduct #correlated #Hubbard #phonon

Abstract: Using numerically exact finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo, we demonstrate that a $B_{1g}$ phonon coupled to the doped $t$-$t'$ repulsive Hubbard model produces genuine $d$-wave superconductivity at a substantial transition temperature, in excess of either interaction alone. The observed trends suggest that stronger Hubbard repulsion may cooperate with the phonon to further raise the pairing scale. The enhancement persists at stronger repulsion within the accessible window, limited by the fermion sign problem, and follows a common trend across phonon frequencies $\Omega$ when organized by a retardation scale $2\pi T/\Omega$. We also find a well-defined superconducting dome in doping, echoing a characteristic feature of correlated superconductors. Our results identify the $B_{1g}$ phonon as a plausible microscopic ingredient for robust $d$-wave superconductivity in the Hubbard model and suggest a concrete, physically motivated route toward materials with higher superconducting transition temperatures.

item.title: [8] Meta-Altermagnetism and Enhanced Spin-Splitting
item.description:
Last authors: Bogeng Wen, Hae-Young Kee

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly relevant theory of altermagnetism, van Hove singularities, and anomalous Hall effects.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #anomalousHall

Abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnets with zero net magnetization and spin-split electronic bands. Here, we explore whether altermagnetism can exhibit a discontinuous jump, a phenomenon we refer to as meta-altermagnetism. We show that meta-altermagnetism can emerge in 2D systems when magnetic-order-induced band reconstruction drives spin-split van Hove singularities (vHSs) across the Fermi level. Using mean-field theory for an extended $t$-$J$ model on a two-sublattice square lattice including anisotropic hopping integral, we find that a first-order meta-altermagnetic transition produces an intermediate altermagnetic regime with reduced staggered magnetization but strongly enhanced magnetic octupole and time-reversal-odd spin-splitter conductivity. We further show that the first-order transition line terminates at a quantum critical endpoint, giving rise to a rich phase diagram as the chemical potential and anisotropic hopping strength are varied. Our results identify the spin split vHSs as a route to enhancing spin-splitter effect for spintronic applications.

item.title: [9] Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid
item.description:
Last authors: Allan MacDonald, Ali Yazdani

Authors: Ryan L. Lee, Jungwoo Lee, Viliam Va\v{n}o, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Ali Yazdani

Tags: #graphene #superconduct #Landaulevel

Abstract: Lattices of quantized vortices are a defining property of rotating superfluids and of type-II superconductors in magnetic fields. Realizing an analogous vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid-formed from bound electron-hole pairs-has remained challenging because excitons are electrically neutral. Building on previous theoretical studies of the low-energy excitations in an exciton superfluid, recent theory has predicted that in a strong magnetic field, a weakly charged exciton superfluid can stabilize a vortex-antivortex lattice arising from the mutual repulsion of fractionally charged vortex cores. Here we report evidence for this predicted vortex lattice in a bilayer exciton condensate by imaging its charged vortices with the scanning tunnelling microscope. The condensate forms between Landau levels of two graphene layers separated by a thin hexagonal boron nitride barrier in a perpendicular magnetic field. We find that the vortex lattice periodicity scales with the total excess charge and is insensitive to its distribution between the two layers, in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Our observations provide evidence for phase coherence in an exciton superfluid system.

item.title: [7] Few-Electron Partitioning in the Fractional Quantum Hall Regime
item.description:
Last authors: J. Rech, B. Gr\'emaud

Authors: T. Jonckheere, J. Rech, B. Gr\'emaud

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental relevance to fractional quantum Hall states and electron partitioning.

Tags: #theory #fractionalquantumHall #statistics

Abstract: Motivated by few-electron partitioning experiments [Shaju et al., Nature 642, 928 (2025)], we study the partition statistics of $N$-electron states at a fractional quantum Hall point contact. At the solvable point $g=1/2$, we obtain nonperturbative current and noise formulas for arbitrary drives, while for Lorentzian pulses (Levitons) the full counting statistics reduces to an $N\times N$ determinant. We show that the charge is transferred solely in units of $e$, and that symmetrized cumulants for $N=2,3,4$ reveal strong antibunching and higher-order correlations, observable in a $(\nu_1,\nu_2)=(1,1/3)$ junction.

item.title: [8] From a Lifshitz Transition to Spin-Density-Wave Order: Sr2RuO4 under Uniaxial Strain
item.description:
Last authors: Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Antoine Georges

Authors: Evgeny A. Stepanov, Sophie Beck, Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Antoine Georges

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strongly correlated electronic structure and Lifshitz transitions in a high-interest material.

Tags: #theory #Sr2RuO4 #Lifshitztransition

Abstract: In recent years, the effects of uniaxial strain on Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ have been extensively investigated, revealing a pronounced enhancement of the superconducting critical temperature accompanied by experimental indications of an emergent magnetically ordered state. In this Letter, we study the impact of strain on the spectral and magnetic properties of this material within an advanced many-body theoretical framework. We find that strain induces an anisotropic Lifshitz transition, which enhances the electron scattering rate along the elongation axis while simultaneously promoting coherent Fermi-liquid behavior in the perpendicular direction, in close agreement with experimental observations. Taking into account this anisotropic behavior allows us to capture the magnetic instability leading to a finite-temperature ordered state at large strain values. Our analysis further reveals that the magnetic response is dominated by two competing wave vectors associated with distinct nesting vectors: one within the $\gamma$ sheet and the other between the $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets of the Fermi surface. Both wave vectors can stabilize magnetic order, with their competition depending sensitively on the coherence of the respective Fermi surface sheets.

item.title: [10] Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum
item.description:
Last authors: Gianluca Stefanucci, Keshav M. Dani

Authors: Xing Zhu, Jacques Hawecker, Enrico Perfetto, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly relevant ARPES study on Floquet-like band engineering in TMDC heterostructures.

Tags: #ARPES #Floquet #heterostructure

Abstract: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

item.title: [7] Charge Filling-Dependent Valley Polarization and its Dynamics Driven by Correlated Interlayer Exciton States in WSe2/WS2 Heterobilayer
item.description:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Kazunari Matsuda

Authors: Zhiwei Li, Haonan Wang, Yubei Xiang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strongly correlated states and Mott physics in moire heterostructures; highly relevant.

Tags: #experiment #moire #Mottphysics

Abstract: Moir\'e heterostructures of transition metal dichalcogenides provide an emerging platform for studying the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states. The valley degree of freedom and its dynamics in the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states in the moir\'e system are crucial for fundamental understanding and applications of valleytronics. Although the strongly correlated states in moir\'e systems have been extensively investigated, their impact on valley degrees of freedom and its dynamics remains unexplored. Here, we study the charge filling-dependent valley relaxation dynamics of interlayer excitons (IXs) in WSe2/WS2 moir\'e heterobilayer system. The evolution of moir\'e IXs dynamics across the Mott transition is elucidated by combining time-resolved optical spectroscopy with Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that the radiative decay and recombination rate of IXs are enhanced at the integer filling factors n (=-1). Moreover, the valley relaxation rate of IXs at n=$\pm$1 is significantly decreased. The resulting reduction in wavefunction overlap and phonon scattering process suppresses the nonradiative recombination and intervalley scattering of IXs. These anomalous behaviors are attributed to the modification of IXs recombination pathways and enhance excitonic coherence due to the localization of introduced charge carriers at integer filling of moir\'e site. Our results explore exciton and valley dynamics as sensitive probes of strongly correlated states in moir\'e systems and highlight possible ways to control excitonic coherence and valleytronic properties in two-dimensional quantum materials.

item.title: [8] The Flexoelectric Twist: Persistence of Heavy Fermion Picture in Small-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Xi Dai, Berthold J\"ack

Authors: Qirong Yao, Ka Cheuk Fan, Tianyu Qiao, Hao Shi, Xi Dai, Berthold J\"ack

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Scanning tunneling microscopy on twisted graphene showing correlated heavy-fermion physics; high experimental interest.

Tags: #STS #graphene #heavyfermion

Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle ($\theta\approx1.05^{\circ}$) hosts flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated and topological phases. At smaller twist angles ($\theta<1^{\circ}$), attice relaxation profoundly alters the moir\'e landscape. The extent to which moir\'e lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices ($\theta\approx0.3-0.7^{\circ}$), we observe a pronounced $dI/dV$ peak at the AA site of the moir\'e lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point, lattice reconstruction over moir\'e lattice length scales, as well as a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites. We demonstrate at a phenomenological level that the inclusion of moir\'e lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion $f-$ states localized at AA sites. The additional inclusion of atomic lattice dilation enerates a strong flexo-electric response that explicitly breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing compact, localized $f$-states at the AA sites down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant $c$-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements quantitatively visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime $\theta<1^{\circ}$. Our findings provide microscopic insights into how flexo-electricity affects the low-energy electronic structure of small-angle TBG. More broadly, our study establishes small-angle TBG as a new class of moir\'e materials to explore the interacting Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the $f-$occupation and $c-$density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.

item.title: [9] Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
item.description:
Last authors: Ziqiang Wang, Jian Wang

Authors: Tianheng Wei, Yanzhao Liu, Wei Ren, Zhen Liang, Ziqiang Wang, Jian Wang

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Scanning Josephson tunneling on iron-based films showing sign-reversal pairing; very relevant to electronic-structure physics.

Tags: #STS #superconductivity #iron-based

Abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.

item.title: [8] Two-Dimensional Magnetic Materials from Ferromagnetism to Altermagnetism: Fabrication, Symmetry, Evidence, and Device Readiness
item.description:
Last authors: Peixin Qin, Zhiqi Liu

Authors: Guojian Zhao, Ziang Meng, Li Liu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Comprehensive review of altermagnetism and 2D magnets; highly relevant to user's topical interest.

Tags: #altermagnet #monolayer #magnetism

Abstract: Atomically thin magnets are governed by composition, thickness, stacking, strain, defects, substrates, ferroic order, and interfaces. This Review organizes two-dimensional (2D) magnetism using net magnetization and momentum-space spin splitting or spin-polarization patterns as primary coordinates, supplemented by sublattice structure and the symmetry relations between opposite-spin sublattices. Ferromagnets generally carry a net moment; ferrimagnets can be fully compensated. Conventional antiferromagnets may retain spin-degenerate bands, while altermagnets permit nonrelativistic alternating spin splitting under dimension-specific symmetry constraints. M1-M4 reporting classes introduced here distinguish layer-resolved atomically thin forms, non-layer-resolved thin flakes or films, bulk benchmarks, and theoretical candidates or design routes; the evidence category and ordering-temperature provenance are reported independently. Current experimental support for altermagnetism comes mainly from M2 thin-film and M3 bulk benchmarks, leaving a fully verified atomically thin M1 altermagnetic phase as an open experimental goal. Most proposed monolayer and few-layer systems therefore fall within M4, and contested cases clarify the measurements needed for phase assignment. Device readiness is compared qualitatively using operating temperature, readout, switching, domain control, stability, scalability, interface sensitivity, and integration difficulty. Reliable phase assignment and device assessment require complementary measurements from the same material form under matched conditions, ideally on the same specimen or in situ.

item.description:
Last authors: Juntao Huo, Guowei Li

Authors: Hanyang Qian, Wen Sun, Juntao Huo, Guowei Li

Why: Highly relevant experimental work on kagome magnets and topological physics; direct interest.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #kagome #topological #magnetism

Abstract: Achieving a large strain response to a small magnetic-field variation remains a challenge in magnetomechanical materials, particularly in topological systems where the coupling between spin reconstruction and lattice deformation remains unclear. Here, we report an anomalous magnetostrictive response associated with field-induced spin reorientation in the topological Kagome magnet TbMn6Sn6. Below its spin-reorientation temperature of 310 K, an in-plane magnetic field induces an abrupt increase in magnetostriction, which exceeds 120 ppm at 240 K. This transition produces a giant differential piezomagnetic coefficient of approximately 5000 ppm T-1, far exceeding the values reported for other topological magnetic materials and commercial FeGa alloys, and placing TbMn6Sn6 among the most field-sensitive magnetostrictive materials. The field position of this peak agrees with the anomalies in magnetization and magnetotransport, demonstrating that the large differential response is tied to field-induced spin reorientation. Thermal expansion also changes across the spin-reorientation boundary. Raman measurements reveal corresponding anomalies in phonon energy and linewidth, indicating that the reorientation modifies the lattice dynamics. The combined results support a mechanism in which competing magnetic anisotropies of the Tb and Mn sublattices, coupled through Tb-Mn exchange, create magnetic configurations with different equilibrium strains. This finding establishes spin reorientation as a route to giant piezomagnetic responses in topological magnets and provides a basis for magnetomechanical sensing and switching near room temperature.

item.title: [8] Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
item.description:
Last authors: Kaihui Liu, Zhipei Sun

Authors: Nianze Shang, Cuiju Yu, Yucai Lin, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experiment on van der Waals superstructures and collective electronic behavior.

Tags: #vanderWaals #experiment #ferroelectricity

Abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies based on van der Waals materials.

item.description:
Last authors: Y. E. Suyolcu, B. Keimer, H. Takagi, P. Reiss

Abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60\% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

Abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed N\'eel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the N\'eel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

item.title: [8] Thermalization-Controlled Superconducting Diode-Like Transport in Disordered Molybdenum and NbN Thin Films
item.description:
Last authors: Sanjay Rai, Edward Prabu Amaladass

Authors: Akhilesh Kumar, Shivani Soni, Gomathi Natarajan, et al.

Why: Experimental study on superconducting diode-like transport in Mo and NbN thin films, relevant to unconventional superconductivity.

Abstract: Superconducting diode effects are characterized by direction-dependent critical currents in the superconducting state. Here, we investigate diode-like transport in 128-nm-thick Mo thin film deposited on Si_SiO2 substrate by DC magnetron sputtering. The thin film exhibit a superconducting transition temperature TC of 5.8 K. Pronounced current-direction asymmetry and hysteresis are observed in current-voltage characteristics measured in a closed-cycle refrigerator. In contrast, the same thin film exhibits a substantially more symmetric response in a 14T cryogenic system with improved sample thermalization. We attribute this strong dependence on the measurement environment to electrothermal effects arising from current-induced Joule heating and finite thermal relaxation. As the current approaches the superconducting-to-resistive switching condition, the emergence of a resistive component leads to a rapid increase in Joule heating, raising the sample temperature and modifying the switching condition. Conversely, during the resistive-to-superconducting transition, residual heating and finite thermal relaxation reduce the switching current. Since P is equal to I2R it is independent of current polarity, the observed asymmetry is not associated with polarity-dependent Joule heating but with the interplay of thermal relaxation, sweep history, and thermal boundary conditions. item.title: [7] Multiple Current Enhancement Regimes and Interaction Induced Re-entrant Transport in a Quasiperiodic Hubbard Ring with Antiferromagnetic Order
item.description:
Last authors: Souvik Roy, Ranjini Bhattacharya

Why: Theoretical study on transport in quasi-1D Hubbard ring with antiferromagnetic order, relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #theory #quasi-1Dmaterials #antiferromagnetism #transport #Hubbardmodel

Abstract: We investigate persistent charge and spin currents in a one-dimensional quantum ring threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm (AB) flux, considering generalized Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper (AAH) modulation with staggered onsite energies and antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering in both the noninteracting and interacting regimes, with the latter treated using a self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean field theory (MFT). At half filling, two distinct current-enhancement peaks emerge as the modulation strength increases, with quasiperiodic hopping modulation playing a crucial role in establishing the two-peak structure within a restricted parameter regime. Spin-resolved bond-current profiles reveal a switch in the dominant spin contribution between the two peaks, while the inverse participation ratio (IPR) and flux-dependent spin-resolved ground-state energies provide complementary insights into the spatial characteristics of the eigenstates and their spin-dependent flux sensitivity. At quarter filling, the spin current exhibits a single enhancement peak, in contrast to the two-peak response observed at half filling. The Hubbard interaction affects the two half-filled peaks differently: it suppresses the primary peak, whereas the secondary peak exhibits a nonmonotonic, re-entrant response, with the current recovering at finite interaction strength. The interacting results are further characterized through the Drude weight, and comparisons with exact diagonalization (ED) and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations for a finite half-filled system support the reliability of the MFT description. item.title: [8] Edge-Plasmon-Induced Magnetization in Higher Chern Insulators
item.description:
Last authors: Thomas L. Schmidt, Eddwi H. Hasdeo

Authors: Prathyush P. Poduval, Rofii, Muhammad S. Ukhtary, Thomas L. Schmidt, Eddwi H. Hasdeo

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of plasmon-induced magnetization in higher Chern insulators, highly relevant to topological materials.

Tags: #topologicalinsulators #Cherninsulator #plasmons #magnetization #theory

Abstract: Higher Chern insulators host multiple dissipationless chiral edge states, one per unit of Chern number. We study the collective plasmon modes of these edge states at a domain wall between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}$ and $-\mathcal{C}$, using a semiclassical model with Coulomb interactions. The plasmon dispersion is linear at long wavelengths, with a velocity that increases linearly with $\mathcal{C}$. As in conventional two-dimensional metals, the edge plasmon generates an elliptically polarized electric field that decays into the bulk and drives electrons in circular orbits, producing a static orbital magnetization (inverse Faraday effect). For topological edge plasmons, the magnetization has a nontrivial spatial profile set by two competing length scales: the finite extent of the edge states and the plasmon wavelength. At fixed edge-charge amplitude, it grows strongly with $\mathcal{C}$. At the domain wall, it approaches a finite plateau at low frequency and decays as $1/\omega^2$ at high frequency. Its temperature dependence is nonmonotonic, with a maximum at an intermediate temperature. These results show how the Chern number controls plasmon-induced magnetization, in contrast to conventional edge plasmons.

item.title: [8] Spin-Polarized Weyl Fermions and Unconventional Spin Transport
item.description:
Last authors: Hongming Weng, Zhijun Wang

Authors: Chenhao Liang, Haohao Sheng, Sheng Zhang, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, Zhijun Wang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory proposing specific 2D material platform for spin-Weyl fermions with experimental transport implications.

Tags: #topological #spintronics #theory #transport #2Dmaterial

Abstract: Large and electrically controllable spin splitting in nonmagnetic materials is highly desirable for condensed-matter physics and spintronics, enabling strongly spin-polarized quasiparticles and unconventional spin transport as well as their electrical control. Here, we establish a general framework for critical spin-polarized Weyl fermions in two-dimensional (2D) nonmagnetic systems. We predict the $\alpha$-Bi-like Group-V puckered-layer family of 2D ferroelectrics as a material platform combining critical spin-Weyl fermions, giant spin splitting, and electrically switchable nonlinear and spin transport. Our calculations reveal exchange-scale spin splitting induced by spin-orbit coupling and a $p$-wave spin texture in the BiAs monolayer. Moreover, BiAs hosts four critical spin-Weyl points, each formed within a single-spin channel. The nearly quantized $\langle S_z\rangle$ is protected by an emergent $S_z$-conservation symmetry in the low-energy limit. The spin-Weyl cones also give rise to unconventional spin-transport phenomena, including a purely out-of-plane Edelstein response and a pronounced spin Nernst effect. Ferroelectric reversal further enables electrical switching of the $p$-wave spin texture and inversion-odd responses, while the tunability of these properties through composition, strain, and magnetic field is also systematically demonstrated across the entire family. These results establish both a general nonmagnetic framework and a promising material platform for exploring critical spin-Weyl physics, nonlinear Hall phenomena, and unconventional spin transport.

item.description:
Last authors: Yuichi Ikuhara, Toshiaki Kato

Authors: Hiroto Ogura, Yuto Tsukidate, Shun Kondo, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental and theoretical study of superconducting interfaces with graphene, relevant to electronic structure.

Tags: #experiment #theory #graphene #superconductivity #heterostructure #electronicstructure

Abstract: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they uniquely yield ballistic, highly transparent contacts to graphene that survive in high-magnetic-field regimes; however, the microscopic origin of this anomalous transparency has remained a long-standing puzzle. Here, we resolve this paradox by revealing that pristine graphene/MoRe interfaces are governed by the classical A15 superconducting phase. Combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy, we demonstrate that as-deposited MoRe spontaneously forms the A15 phase in direct contact with graphene, whereas thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure that severely degrades the Josephson transparency. Crucially, the one-dimensional (1D) transition-metal atomic chains unique to the A15 structure exhibit a near-perfect lattice match (mismatch < 1%) with graphene edges. First-principles calculations further prove that the d-orbitals of these historically renowned 1D chains possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone near the K point. These findings not only uncover the structural and electronic origins of optimal MoRe contacts but also establish A15-phase superconductors as a geometrically ideal, universal platform for realizing robust quantum electronics based on 2D materials.

item.description:
Last authors: Michael Sch\"uler, Samuel Beaulieu

Authors: Sotirios Fragkos, Ann Chantal Goutier, Umberto Dellasette, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct experimental observation using TR-ARPES of light-induced topological state in graphene.

Abstract: Driving quantum materials with light can reshape not only their electronic band structures but also the geometry of their electronic wavefunctions. In graphene, circularly polarized light is predicted to open gaps at the Dirac points and induce a pseudospin texture and Berry curvature characteristic of the Haldane model, realizing a Floquet Chern insulator. Transport and all-optical measurements have provided evidence for a light-induced anomalous Hall response, but cannot resolve the underlying electronic states in both energy and momentum space. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy has revealed Floquet-Bloch sidebands and hybridization gaps at crossings between Floquet bands. However, these experiments used linearly polarized driving, which preserves time-reversal symmetry and thus does not induce a topological phase. Here, we combine circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy with ab initio theory to investigate graphene driven by circularly polarized light. We observe a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, in agreement with our calculations. These results link the measured dichroic response to the light-induced pseudospin texture and its associated Berry curvature, providing spectroscopic evidence for the Floquet-engineered topological insulating state in graphene.

Abstract: The microscopic origin of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in cuprates remains an outstanding puzzle due to the interplay of intertwined orders. item.description:

item.description:
Last authors: Amit Kanigel, Beena Kalisky

Authors: Shalev Gur, Sajilesh K. P., Shubam Purwar, et al.

Why: High interest vdW material 4Hb-TaS2 involving unconventional superconductivity and hidden orders.

Abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. The van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 provides such a case, combining superconductivity, charge-order tendencies, strong scattering, and magnetic memory manifested through spontaneous vortices. item.description:
Last authors: Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan

Authors: Yichi Zhang, Yiyu Xia, Zhongdong Han, et al.

Abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moir\'e semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moir\'e Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a low-temperature anisotropic phase accompanied by a Fermi surface reconstruction. Near the stripe-to-superconductor transition, we also observed an additional thermodynamic phase transition from metallic stripes to pinned insulating stripes. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moir\'e materials.

Abstract: Understanding the normal state of unconventional superconductors is central to uncovering the origin of superconductivity itself. Unconventional superconductivity often emerges from correlated electronic states characterized by intertwined symmetry-breaking orders. A striking example is 4Hb-TaS2, whose superconducting state exhibits a remarkable range of phenomena, including an unusual magnetic memory effect. Previous experiments showed that magnetic memory can be encoded above Tc and later revealed through spontaneous vortices below Tc, suggesting time-reversal symmetry breaking. However, since memory and vorticity are intertwined, this prevents establishing whether the effect results from trapped flux, weak conventional magnetism, or a true hidden electronic order. Our results rule out explanations based on trapped vortices. Furthermore, the spatial profile of the flux generated by trained samples at zero field is inconsistent with conventional weak magnetism, suggesting a hidden electronic phase that imprints an effective flux on the superconducting condensate.

item.description:
Last authors: Yoichi Ando, Jakob Schluck

Authors: Christoph Wassmer, Ella Nikodem, Oliver Breunig, Yongjian Wang, Yoichi Ando, Jakob Schluck

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental TI-based Majorana platform study involving magnetotransport.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #experiment #topologicalinsulator #Majorana

Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions have recently attracted substantial attention. The ability to study Andreev bound states in a multi-phase parameter space opens up exciting avenues for generating topologically non-trivial phases in superconducting devices. A particularly interesting case is the trijunction based on a topological insulator (TI), which is predicted to host Majorana zero modes for suitable phase configurations (Fu and Kane, PRL 2008). Here we turn to the platform of the side-contacted TI trijunction and present experimental evidence for a multiterminal Josephson effect. We study the transport properties and find typical features of a two-dimensional critical current contour (CCC) as well as bias regimes in which only a single junction remains dissipationless. We pay particular attention to these features and study the effects of magnetic fields on single junctions within the trijunction, where, depending on the field direction, the supercurrents show Fraunhofer patterns, SQUID oscillations, or a monotonic decay. We find good agreement with semiclassical simulations for a single TI junction that take into account the top and bottom surface states. We observe pronounced non-convex shape deformations of the CCC under perpendicular magnetic fields that reflect the flux buildup in the loop formed by our trijunctions and provide a simple model sufficient to explain the observed effect. Our results provide the foundations for future studies of Majorana zero modes on this platform.

item.description:

Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) plays a pivotal role in a broad range of phenomena in condensed matter physics. The recently developed spin space group theory offers a new perspective for characterizing the fundamental symmetry-breaking features of SOC-related phenomena, yet its full potential remains to be explored. Here, we provide a general framework that relates the SOC-induced symmetry breaking to modifications of physical properties and emergence of new physical effects. This approach incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group (OSSG) formalism, which can explicitly describe the symmetry reduction induced by SOC. By parameterizing the SOC Hamiltonian using a SOC tensor that connects real and spin spaces, an expansion in terms of the SOC components can be constructed for the response tensor describing any physical quantity. This framework determines not only whether a SOC-induced response is symmetry allowed, but also the lowest order in SOC at which it emerges and its dependence on magnetic anisotropy. As representative applications, we analyze the magnetoelectric coupling in Type-II multiferroics and show that magnetically induced electric polarization in different systems can be the result of SOC effects of different orders, and can exhibit varying characteristics of magnetic anisotropy. We further apply this theory to the anomalous Hall effect and spin magnetization in antiferromagnets, demonstrating that their distinct transformation properties under the OSSG allow a large anomalous Hall response to coexist with weak spin magnetization. A high-throughput analysis of materials in the MAGNDATA database identifies several symmetry-based material classes favorable for this coexistence. Overall, the proposed framework provides a unified symmetry description of SOC-induced phenomena and offers a systematic way for the identification of SOC-driven functional materials.

Abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Abstract: New insights into the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$ below 50 K are revealed through specific-heat, thermal-expansion and magnetic measurements. The latent heats of the two successive magnetic transitions, together with an improved description of the lattice contribution, enable a detailed determination of the thermal variation of the magnetic entropy. Immediately above the first-order magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N = 6.7$ K), the magnetic entropy per Pr$^{3+}$ is close to that of a doublet, instead of the triplet crystal-field ground state identified by inelastic neutron scattering. This is reminiscent of the CeB$_6$ case and, similarly, strongly suggests a dynamical splitting of the crystal-field ground state within the boron cage. Further evidence of this splitting is provided by the analysis of the low-temperature paramagnetic susceptibility, which resembles that of a non-magnetic ground state. In addition, a large thermal-expansion anomaly is observed below 20 K, consistent with the expected centrifugal Jahn-Teller effect.

item.description:
Last authors: Jeroen van den Brink, Maia G. Vergniory

item.title: [7] Time Reflection-Refraction Crossover at Topological Kramers Edge States
item.description:
Last authors: Junpeng Hou, Ya-Jie Wu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory relevant for topological insulator edge states under time-dependent modulation.

Tags: #topology #edgestates #quantumHall

Abstract: Time-reversal symmetry protects helical edge states against static nonmagnetic backscattering. We show that spatially uniform temporal modulation produces a time reflection-refraction crossover within the same quantum spin Hall phase while preserving time-reversal symmetry of the instantaneous Hamiltonian. A finite gap to the bulk and an edge splitting that vanishes at the Kramers crossing allow the modulation to suppress bulk excitation while remaining nonadiabatic between the edge channels. Virtual transitions through bulk states enable coherent conversion between counter-propagating edge channels at fixed crystal momentum. Near the crossing, $qT$ governs the leading crossover dynamics for a fixed ramp shape, where $q$ is the momentum offset and $T$ the ramp duration. Coherent interference can suppress and restore reflection as the ramp slows. In the adiabatic limit, two initially time-reversed wave packets follow their respective propagation branches and acquire equal geometric displacements. Their group-velocity contributions cancel, isolating the contribution from the Berry curvature to be directly observable. Temporal modulation thus controls protected states and quantum geometry along a topological edge.

item.title: [9] Chiral p-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moir\'e Chern Band
item.description:
Last authors: Yunze Ouyang, Fengcheng Wu

Why: Directly relevant to moire Chern bands, superconductivity, and CDW interplay in twisted MoTe2.

Tags: #moire #superconductivity #CDW #Cherninsulator

Abstract: We study a spin-polarized moir'e Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling $ u=2/3$ and a topological charge density wave at $ u=3/4$. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over $0.7\lesssim u\lesssim0.77$, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral $p$-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.

item.title: [9] Light-Cone Friedel Oscillations: a Window into van Hove Superconductivity
item.description:
Last authors: Vladislav Poliakov, Leonid Levitov

Authors: Archisman Panigrahi, Vladislav Poliakov, Leonid Levitov

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct STM proposal for probing van Hove superconductivity relevant to kagome or moire systems.

Tags: #STM #superconductivity #vanHove #Friedeloscillations

Abstract: Van Hove (vH) singularities can enhance superconductivity by generating a large pairing susceptibility. Yet, it remains challenging to experimentally establish whether pairing really occurs near these points. We show that the saddle-point dispersion near a vH point gives rise to a `light-cone' vH-selective behavior of Friedel oscillations, which is drastically different from the familiar concentric circles. Each vH point maps onto its own real-space light-cone sector, allowing STM around a single impurity to measure whether---and how strongly---that saddle-point quasiparticle sector is gapped. A superconducting gap near vH points suppresses the oscillations in the directions corresponding to peaks in the gap function angular dependence, a behavior that provides a signature of vH-related pairing at STM-accessible length scales. This STM protocol, targeting vH superconductivity, is capable of determining whether superconducting pairing emerges near the vH points or elsewhere on the Fermi surface.

item.title: [8] Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
item.description:
Last authors: Ya-Hui Zhang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High relevance to twisted MoTe2 and fractional Chern/quantum Hall physics.

Tags: #quantumHall #superconductivity #anyon #moire

Abstract: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ is a long-standing open problem, with renewed interest from the recent observations of fractional Chern insulators. In this work we construct variational wavefunctions that build in the exact anyon statistics and combine theory-guided composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton wavefunctions with neural-network correlations on the sphere. For spinless and SU(2) semions we confirm the paired anyon superfluid, well below the best crystal states. At $\theta=\pi/3$ liquids and crystals are closer in energy for the spinless case. For $\theta=\pi/3$ anyons with SU(3) flavor, we find two candidates. One is a skyrmion Hall crystal, in which the anyons form an integer quantum Hall state in the effective magnetic field from the spin texture. The other is a chiral color superconductor of six-anyon clusters, the color-flavor-locked pairing descendant of a holon metal with SU(3) color gauge symmetry and SU(3) flavor symmetry; its wavefunction is a hyperdeterminant rather than a product of parton determinants. Within our variational ansatz the color superconductor has better energy than both crystals and the color-flavor locked phases with U(1)$^2$ and Z$_3$ gauge groups. For twisted MoTe$_2$ this suggests that the reentrant integer quantum anomalous Hall phase is the skyrmion Hall crystal of the doped anyons, and that the observed superconductivity may be the color superconductor, which can undergo a transition to an $f+if$ BCS superconductor with a jump of the chiral central charge by 3.

item.description:
Last authors: Bo Xu, Tim Thomay

Authors: Chiran Wijesundara, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, Yuan Lu, Herbert Fotso, Bo Xu, Tim Thomay

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin injection/transport; relevant for understanding spin-polarized transport systems.

Tags: #experiment #ferromagnet

Abstract: Electrically spin-injected ensembles of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots emit circularly polarized single photons, with the emission helicity determined by the spin polarization of the injected electrons. A ferromagnetic CoFeB spin-injection layer with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, combined with an MgO tunnel barrier, enables spin-polarized electron injection into the quantum-dot active region, resulting in circularly polarized photon emission at zero applied magnetic field. These devices realize direct spin-charge-photon conversion in an electrically driven, microelectronics-compatible quantum light source that operates without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors and time-tagged readout, we measure time-resolved photon-number statistics that resolve up to $|2\rangle$ Fock states within a single excitation cycle. While single-photon ($n=|1\rangle$) emission tracks the electrical excitation pulse as expected, the two-photon ($n=|2\rangle$) statistics exhibit pronounced fluctuations at multiple temporal positions within the pulse. These fluctuations vanish upon demagnetization of the spin-injection layer, establishing a direct link between the multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers. The observations indicate that spin injection controls not only the helicity of the emitted photons but also higher-order temporal correlations of the emission. The behavior is phenomenologically captured by inserting both a variable excitation mechanism and a set of multi-emitter collapse operators within a stochastic wave function evolution. The platform thus opens a route to electrically driven, spin-controlled single and multi-photon Fock-state sources and provides a testbed for spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources.

item.description:
Last authors: Frances Hellman, Sin\'ead M. Griffin

Authors: Temuujin Bayaraa, Subhashree Satapathy, Peter Fischer, Frances Hellman, Sin\'ead M. Griffin

Why: Interesting topological magnetism in amorphous materials; relevant to broader interest in magnetic topology.

Abstract: Topological phases in solids are typically associated with crystalline symmetry and periodic order. Recent work has shown, however, that reciprocal-space topology can persist even in amorphous materials. Whether real-space topology, encoded directly in magnetic textures, can emerge without crystalline symmetry remains unresolved. Here, we show that structural disorder itself can generate the interactions required to stabilize topological spin textures in amorphous FeGe. Using first-principles calculations to construct a statistical magnetic Hamiltonian, we find that local structural asymmetry and broad distributions of exchange couplings produce a frustrated magnetic network with net ferromagnetic character rather than spin-glass freezing, supporting vortex-, antivortex-, and skyrmion-like textures that self-organize into emergent spin superstructures. Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental Curie temperature and show that these textures persist even when Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and anisotropy terms are suppressed. In contrast, homogenizing the Hamiltonian strongly suppresses the topological response, identifying bond-to-bond heterogeneity as the essential ingredient. Our results show that real-space topology in a magnet need not be inherited from crystalline chirality, but can emerge from disorder itself.

Abstract: A recent experiment [Cohen et al., Science 382, 542 (2023)] observed a robustly quantized $e^2/2h$ conductance in a quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall edges (a quantum Hall transformer), which then vanishes at low temperature. item.title: [8] Thermal Strain-Driven Periodic Ripples in Ultrathin Sb2Te3/Graphene Heterostructures and their Implications for Strain Engineering
item.description:
Last authors: Valentina Gallardo, Carolina Parra

Authors: Francisco Munoz, Manuel Fuenzalida, Paula Mellado, et al.

Why: Heterostructure research and strain engineering of electronic band structure in topological materials.

Abstract: We report the observation of a highly regular, periodic ripple superstructure with a characteristic wavelength of approximately 8.7 nm in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of ultrathin Sb2Te3 epitaxially grown on monolayer graphene. We attribute this structural modulation to an extrinsic, thermally driven mechanism: upon post-growth cooling, the opposite signs of the thermal expansion coefficients of the bulk SiO2 substrate and the graphene layer generate interfacial strain that drives the formation of ripples. In this ultrathin thickness regime, the Sb2Te3 film conforms to the buckled graphene morphology without delamination, because the interfacial van der Waals adhesion energy exceeds the elastic energy cost associated with bending. Furthermore, based on density functional theory and effective low-energy model calculations, we predict that this structural corrugation leads to substantial modifications of the electronic band structure. item.description:
Last authors: Doried Ghader, Bilal Jabakhanji

Abstract: Hybridization between bosonic excitations can produce topological bands, but their Chern numbers conceal how constituent modes generate the resulting Berry geometry. The latter couples momentum-space variations of the sector imbalance to a gauge-invariant relative Berry connection and has an equivalent gauge-covariant pseudospin representation. item.title: [7] Dynamic Behaviors of Materials Under Angle-Resolved Experiments: A Matrix Framework for Nonlinear Physics
item.description:
Last authors: Xuan Ye, Teng Ma

Authors: Hongjin Xiong, Zhonghui Xia, Xuan Ye, Teng Ma

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: General framework for dynamic angle-resolved experiments, demonstrated on WTe2, potentially useful for data interpretation.

Tags: #methodology #nonlinearoptics #WTe2 #topologicalsemimetal #experiment

Abstract: Matter and external stimuli interact dynamically almost everywhere in nature. Under an applied field, a material seldom stays in the state in which it was characterized, and its properties change with time. Angle-resolved experiments are the standard way to resolve direction-dependent properties, however, current theoretical tools for data analysis are built for static states, leaving dynamic behaviors largely neglected. Here, we develop a generalized ``input-coefficient-output'' (ICO) approach that constructs spatial operation matrices and symmetry-reduced coefficient matrices across diverse physical systems, as we verify for nonlinear optics, elasticity, electrostriction and magnetostriction, and a Python program is released for convenient application. Using angle-resolved polarized second-harmonic generation (SHG) as an example, we focus on the dynamic modeling of material properties under angle-dependent stimuli, construct dynamic matrix equations that capture the time-dependent evolution of material responses, and propose three dynamic models and a point-to-point data fitting method. For the SHG experiments performed on $T_d-$WTe$_2$, the discrete dynamic model captures the asymmetric characteristics of the measured polar pattern with a significantly improved coefficient of determination ($R^2$ increasing from 0.567 to 0.773), whereas conventional static models are constrained to a symmetric curve. The evolution operator extracted from the dynamic model connects the macroscopic measurement to microscopic intermediate states during their interaction with stimuli. This work provides a practical matrix framework for dynamic modeling of material properties, paving the way for exploring complex nonlinear physics under realistic experimental conditions.

Abstract: The ultrastrong coupling regime of cavity photons and quantum materials has emerged as a pathway to modify materials properties, however definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Abstract: Boosting superconductivity by metallic reservoirs is the essence of Kivelson's bilayer proposal. One layer provides pairing to the electrons, while the weakly coupled metal provides additional phase coherence to those pairs by mediating extended-range pair-pair coupling. Demonstrating significant and unambiguous performance gains with strong-coupling methods for such set-ups had been difficult. Abstract: High-temperature superconductivity in pressurized and thin-film nickelates has generated intense interest, yet magnetism in their ambient-pressure parent phases remains poorly understood, despite its potentially crucial role in pairing. item.description:
Last authors: Junwei Liu, Binghai Yan

Abstract: Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between electron and hole Fermi surfaces fundamentally reshapes this competition. This mismatch stabilizes FFLO-like electron-hole pairing and drives spontaneous symmetry breaking of the EI state. The resulting symmetry breaking reconstructs the pairing phase space for SC and EI state, such that different regions of the Fermi surface complementarily support either EI or SC correlations, leading to a natural coexistence of the two orders. item.description:
Last authors: Dieter Koelle, Wolfgang Lang

Authors: Bernd Aichner, Simon Koch, Philipp A. Korner, et al.

Abstract: Focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation with 30-keV ions is a key tool for nanoscale patterning and defect engineering in high transition temperature (Tc) cuprate superconducting devices, yet its usable fluence window is constrained by the competing requirements of reliable superconductivity suppression and minimal structural degradation. In this work, we provide a comprehensive dataset on the effects of large-area 30-keV He+ ion exposure on the electric transport and superconducting properties of epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7 (YBCO) thin films. X-ray diffraction shows a fluence-driven loss of crystalline order accompanied by an out-of-plane lattice expansion and an orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition, culminating in predominant amorphization at the highest fluence of 1 x 10^16 cm^-2. Raman spectra exhibit increasing disorder while lacking signatures of oxygen depletion, indicating that irradiation mainly generates oxygen-related Frenkel defects rather than changing the carrier concentration. Consistently, with increasing fluence, the normal-state resistivity \rho_N(T) at temperature T above Tc increases strongly, while d \rho_N/d T remains nearly unchanged at moderate fluence. The suppression of Tc is accurately described by Abrikosov-Gor'kov pair breaking and reaches complete quenching of superconductivity at 4.5 x 10^15 cm^-2. The anisotropic upper critical fields decrease approximately exponentially with increasing fluence, the vortex activation energy is reduced, and the anisotropy drops, in contrast to oxygen-depleted YBCO. Hall-angle analysis confirms a nearly constant carrier density but a systematic increase in defect scattering and reduced mobility, consistent with a crossover toward the dirty limit at high fluence. These results establish quantitative fluence thresholds and a practical operational window for He-FIB nanopatterning of YBCO quantum circuits.

item.description:
Last authors: Tabin Dharanikota, Lukasz Fidkowski

Tags: #theory #Diracfermions #Luttingerliquid

Abstract: We construct an exactly solvable Hamiltonian lattice model realizing a 1+1d Dirac fermion, with exact microscopic vector and axial vector $U(1)$ symmetries. The mixed anomaly between these is accommodated by the not-on-site action of the symmetries. Our Hilbert space is a $Z_2$-graded tensor product of local $Z_2$-graded Hilbert spaces which include infinite dimensional rotor degrees of freedom. At the free Dirac fixed point, our Hamiltonian contains irrelevant interactions, which we compute to leading order.

item.description:
Last authors: Juraj Krempasky, Petr Nemec

Authors: Zeynab Sadeghi, Tomas Ostatnicky, Eva Schmoranzerova, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Interplay of Rashba SOC and magnetism in a specific material; relevant to spin-orbit physics interests.

Tags: #experiment #Rashba #magnetism

Abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amplitude and coercive field of the pump-induced change in ellipticity hysteresis loops, is attributed to laser-induced modifications of the ferroelectric sublattice displacement, which affect the ferroelectric polarization and the associated Rashba spin-orbit interaction. While the first type of optical spin-orbit torque has already been observed in the diluted magnetic semiconductor (Ga,Mn)As, the second effect is unique to the multiferroic Rashba semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te, opening new opportunities for all-optical manipulation of magnetic order and spin-orbit torque generation in spin-orbitronic devices.

item.title: [7] Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
item.description:
Last authors: Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari

Authors: Matteo Quinzi, Andrea Pintus, Tommaso Chiarotti, Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of spectral functions (ARPES observable) showing pseudogap and Fermi arcs in Hubbard model.

Tags: #theory #Hubbard-model #pseudogap

Abstract: Strongly correlated solids exhibit phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories, with the associated self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. In the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model, we find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet develops, in addition to long-range ordered stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces of convoluted shape, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such a complex phenomenon, where a pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and their metallic interfaces.

item.description:

Why: Direct relevance to kagome systems and vdW monolayers with topological flat bands and Chern phases.

Tags: #theory #kagome #van-der-Waals

Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moir\'e materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.

Abstract: Mn$_2$Au is one of the most promising materials for antiferromagnetic spintronics due to its high N\'eel temperature, moderate anisotropy, layered spin structure allowing current induced spin-orbit-torques, and ultrafast spin dynamics. Further understanding and control of the magnetic order in Mn$_2$Au for ultrafast spintronics applications via ultrashort electric/optical means requires accurate understanding of how its magnetic properties depend on temperature. Here we present atomistic spin dynamics simulations of the temperature-dependent macroscopic magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au single crystals. We introduce a spin Hamiltonian based on previous ab initio calculations which produces temperature-dependent scaling of the anisotropy constants with magnetisation consistent with Zener-Akulov-Callen-Callen power laws. Our model provides an understanding of temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au that enables large-scale simulation of the working conditions of spintronic devices.

These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM states result from symmetry and can also emerge in other QCs.

Abstract: Our goal is to provide precise effective operators for monolayer graphene at Fermi energy. We consider the microscopic potential created by a lattice, and add a macroscopic potential with the same periodicity but varying at a scale $\varepsilon^{-1} \in \mathbb{N}$, creating a superlattice. Our approach combines a variational approximation with perturbation theory and a multiscale method. At the effective level the usual massless Dirac operator is enriched by other operators. We provide simulations for graphene to show the increased accuracy, and a theoretical result proving the improved validity time scale in the dynamical case.
